body.x: Autonomous mobile robots are becoming more common across factories, yet most still rely heavily on LiDAR and cameras to determine their position on the floor. These systems can lose track of a robot's location in dust, steam, or smoke, limiting automation in industries such as steel, chemicals, and food processing. In the global steel industry, 36% of accidents occur under low-visibility conditions, and in the United Kingdom's food and drink industry, such conditions account for 25% of casualties.
If a robot could keep its bearings even when it cannot see, plants in these industries could automate operations that still depend on workers moving through hazardous, low-visibility areas today.

body.cap: MilliTrack AMR Plus Tracker provides 3 cm localization accuracy at distances of up to 30 meters and supports multiple industrial interfaces | Photo - MilliTrack

body.x: MilliTrack Co., Ltd., a spin-off from the Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST), is addressing that gap with AMR+, a radio frequency (RF) localization add-on that helps autonomous mobile robots maintain positioning accuracy in low-visibility industrial environments. The system is installed in two parts: an AMR+ Tracker mounted on the robot, and AMR+ Tags placed only in the specific low-visibility zones where the AMR's optical sensors fail, with no network or power cabling required. According to MilliTrack, installation takes only minutes, and AMR+ integrates with an AMR's existing localization stack, leaving current workflows largely unchanged.

MilliTrack says AMR+ addresses that gap with its patented millimeter-wave technology, protected by 22 patents, which delivers 3 cm localization accuracy over a 30 m range even in environments dense with metal structures and machinery — a level of precision the company describes as the best among RF localization products on the market. AMR+ also provides collision avoidance that meets the IEC TS61496-5 safety standard.

body.cap: MilliTrack AMR Plus Tag requires no network or power cabling and offers up to 20 years of battery life | Photo - MilliTrack

body.x: MilliTrack was founded by CEO Songmin Kim, a KAIST professor with more than 15 years of experience in mobile sensing research, as a university spin-off. The company's core localization technology has won 11 awards, including multiple Best Paper Awards at the Association for Computing Machinery's MobiSys conference. According to MilliTrack, its localization system is already deployed at multiple global enterprises in heavy industry and manufacturing, with more than 30 ongoing proof-of-concept projects spanning robotics, automotive and smart factory applications.

Beyond safety, MilliTrack highlights the operational costs of losing localization. Remapping an AMR fleet after a facility layout change can take up to an hour, at an average loss of USD 260,000 per instance, according to the company. Because Tag-based localization is unaffected by drift or layout changes, MilliTrack says AMR+ removes much of that remapping overhead. AMR+ Tags require no network or power cabling and run up to 20 years on a single battery, according to the company. The company is targeting plant operators in heavy industries, chemicals and food processing, along with the broader dust- and steam-exposed manufacturing sectors — including chemicals, food and beverage, petroleum and coal, and wood — that together account for nearly 50% of U.S. manufacturing.

body.cap: MilliTrack AMR Plus deployment process, from mounting the tracker and installing tags to automatic configuration and operation | Photo - MilliTrack

body.x: MilliTrack is positioning AMR+ as a retrofit option for plant operators looking to expand automation without replacing their existing AMR fleets, and says it is seeking partnerships with AMR manufacturers, robotics system integrators and industrial automation providers as it expands into global manufacturing and logistics markets. The company projects that AMR+ could reach more than 200,000 units in adoption and USD 1.5 billion in revenue, citing the size of the dust- and steam-exposed manufacturing market as its addressable opportunity — figures MilliTrack presents as its own outlook rather than independently verified market data.

MilliTrack submitted AMR+ for the CES 2027 Innovation Awards in the Construction & Industrial Tech, Embedded Technologies, Robotics, and Supply & Logistics categories, and the company will exhibit at CES 2027 with a dedicated booth.
